citation: 'The Court-House before the fire', wood engraving, in A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 2 (Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885), p. 65.
author: Engraver unnamed (signed by the engraving company at lower left)
describes_date: 1870-1871, the Court House as enlarged, before the fire
repository: Internet Archive, item historyofchicago02andr (scan leaf 67). The plate is committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3688/andreas_v2_p65_court_house_before_the_fire.jpg.
locator: Vol. 2, p. 65, the oval engraving at the head of the page: the Court House from the south-east (Clark and Washington Streets), the east wing nearest at right showing its south and east fronts, the 1853 house with its south portico and steps, the cupola under a flag, the west wing beyond at left.
rights_note: Published 1885 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-19 (T-3688) from the Internet Archive's page image of leaf 67 (2306 x 3299 px); the engraving cropped and committed, sha256 a6a2476a950e5cbdc5e5ff9d45736b78546a39b7c80125124a3cdcb2777c170d.
note: An engraving made for the 1885 history, most likely from a photograph, fourteen years after the building burned; it agrees with the 1871 stereograph on the wings, crests and domes, and shows the south and east fronts the stereograph does not.
what_it_supplies: the Court House's south and east fronts, drawn
the south portico and its steps
